name: Sanofi S.A.
overview: Sanofi is a French biopharmaceutical company that, after divesting a 50% controlling stake in its Consumer Healthcare business (Opella, home to Doliprane and Allegra) to CD&R for roughly EUR10.4bn in December 2024 and spinning off its API manufacturing arm (EUROAPI) in 2022, is now a focused, pure-play prescription biopharma organized around Immunology, Rare Disease, Neurology, Oncology and Vaccines. The company's growth is dominated by Dupixent (dupilumab), a blockbuster IL-4Ra antibody co-developed and profit-shared with Regeneron that generated roughly EUR15.7bn of sales in FY2025 (~36% of group revenue), alongside a fast-growing cohort of post-2019 launches (ALTUVIIIO, Beyfortus, Ayvakit, Sarclisa, Tzield, Wayrilz, Qfitlia) and a global vaccines franchise (influenza, RSV/Beyfortus, meningitis, travel and pediatric vaccines). Sanofi trades on Euronext Paris (SAN.PA) and as an ADR on Nasdaq (SNY), with roughly 51% of 2025 sales in the US, 21% in Europe and 28% in the rest of the world.

business_model.summary: Sanofi earns the large majority of profit from patent-protected biologics and specialty drugs sold to healthcare systems (payers, hospitals, specialty pharmacies) and physicians, supplemented by a vaccines business sold largely to governments and public health systems. Dupixent is shared 50/50 in profit (not just royalty) with Regeneron in the US, which shows up as a large and growing 'profit sharing' deduction in other operating income/expenses; Beyfortus is similarly partnered with AstraZeneca. The FY2025 divestiture of Opella removed the company's only meaningful B2C/OTC consumer revenue stream, so essentially all remaining revenue is B2B/institutional (payers, providers, governments) and recurring in the sense that chronic biologic therapies (Dupixent, ALTUVIIIO, enzyme-replacement rare-disease drugs) generate durable, multi-year patient revenue, while vaccines are more seasonal/tender-based and general medicines are in structural decline as products lose exclusivity or are divested.

revenue_streams.name: Rare Disease (Ayvakit, ALTUVIIIO, Cerezyme, Fabrazyme, Nexviazyme, Xenpozyme)
Other pharma launches since 2019 (Sarclisa, Tzield, Wayrilz, Qfitlia, Rezurock, Cablivi)
Other/General Medicines (legacy branded and off-patent products, incl. Aubagio genericized)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/institutional — payers, hospitals, specialty pharmacies, physicians and national immunization programs; no meaningful direct-to-consumer business post-Opella divestiture
business_model.geographic_mix: US ~51%, Europe ~21%, Rest of World ~28% (based on FY2025 sales of EUR43,626m)

main_competitors: Regeneron (partner and, in adjacent indications, potential competitor)
competitive_position.market_position: Top-10 global pharma by revenue; #1 or #2 position in several niches — global leader in influenza vaccines and infant RSV prevention (Beyfortus), the dominant IL-4/IL-13 biologic in atopic dermatitis/asthma/related type-2 inflammatory diseases via Dupixent, and a leading position in lysosomal storage disorders (Gaucher, Fabry) and hemophilia (ALTUVIIIO) following the 2025 Blueprint Medicines (Ayvakit, systemic mastocytosis) acquisition.

moat_factors.factor: Dupixent franchise breadth and switching costs
moat_factors.description: Nine-plus approved indications (atopic dermatitis, asthma, CRSwNP, EoE, prurigo nodularis, COPD, bullous pemphigoid, CSU) built on a decade of trial data and physician familiarity; >1.5m patients globally create durable prescriber habit and payer formulary inertia.

Deep co-development/co-commercialization relationship gives Sanofi access to a best-in-class R&D engine (also source of the Amvuttra royalty stream via Alnylam-adjacent deals) but also means Sanofi shares roughly half of US Dupixent profit rather than capturing it outright.

moat_factors.factor: Vaccine manufacturing scale and regulatory barriers
moat_factors.description: High capital intensity, biologics manufacturing complexity, and government-tender relationships make vaccines a durable but low-growth moat; few competitors can match Sanofi's global influenza and combination-vaccine manufacturing footprint.

Long-standing leadership in Gaucher/Fabry (via Genzyme heritage) and now hemophilia (ALTUVIIIO) and systemic mastocytosis (Ayvakit) benefits from small, high-touch patient populations and specialist prescriber relationships, though gene-therapy competitors threaten multi-year annuity economics in Fabry/Gaucher long-term.

moat_factors.factor: Brand/scale in emerging markets and government relationships
moat_factors.description: Longstanding presence in China and emerging markets and Global Health Unit access programs support volume in lower-margin geographies.

weaknesses: Extreme concentration in a single molecule (Dupixent, ~36% of sales and the majority of recent sales growth)
Profit-sharing with Regeneron caps Sanofi's economic capture of its most important growth driver
General Medicines/legacy portfolio in structural decline, masking underlying growth in headline consolidated numbers
Weak recent late-stage pipeline conversion — tolebrutinib CRL, amlitelimab discontinuation, itepekimab and balinatunfib discontinuations, riliprubart CIDP study stopped, all within 2025-2026
Persistent valuation discount to large-cap US pharma and even some EU peers (Novo Nordisk, AstraZeneca, Eli Lilly), reflecting the market's skepticism about post-Dupixent growth

growth_drivers: Dupixent lifecycle management: additional indications (CSU in children, bullous pemphigoid, allergic fungal rhinosinusitis under US review) and potential Q4W higher-dose/co-formulation convenience upgrades; 2030 sales ambition raised to ~EUR25bn (from ~EUR22bn) at the July 2026 upgrade

Post-2019 launch cohort scaling fast: launches were ~13% of Q2-2026 sales, +61% YoY, led by Ayvakit (systemic mastocytosis, from the ~$9.5bn 2025 Blueprint Medicines acquisition), ALTUVIIIO (hemophilia A switches) and Sarclisa (now with a subcutaneous CirCLIQ formulation)

Vaccines pipeline expansion: Fluzone HD label expansion (50+ age group under review), next-gen RSV+HMPV combination vaccine, yellow fever and pneumococcal programs, plus the pending/closed Dynavax acquisition (HEPLISAV-B hepatitis B vaccine, closed Feb-2026) adding an adult-vaccines platform and shingles candidate

Business operating margin expansion — business gross margin +3.7pp in Q2-2026 (81.2% vs 77.5%) on mix and cost discipline; management guiding to continued margin increase and 'sustained profitable growth with increased focus on cash generation' under the new CEO

Capital return: buybacks (EUR5bn completed 2025, EUR1bn 2026 tranche completed by end-April) shrinking share count roughly 2-3%/year, plus the 32nd consecutive year of dividend growth expected for FY2026
Disciplined bolt-on M&A funded by Opella proceeds — Blueprint Medicines, Vigil Neuroscience, Dynavax — expanding Rare Disease and Vaccines platforms rather than paying down debt

business.risk: Dupixent concentration and eventual patent cliff
business.description: Roughly 36% of group sales and the large majority of recent growth rides on one molecule; while core US composition-of-matter and method patents are described as running from 2031 to 2045, the scale of the eventual loss of exclusivity dwarfs anything else in the portfolio and biosimilar competitors will target it aggressively as key patents approach expiry.

business.risk: Direct competition in Dupixent's core indications
business.description: Eli Lilly's lebrikizumab (Ebglyss) and LEO Pharma's tralokinumab (Adbry) are taking share in atopic dermatitis with a more targeted IL-13 mechanism; Amgen/AstraZeneca's tezepelumab (Tezspire) competes in severe asthma. Dupixent still holds ~70%+ share of atopic dermatitis biologics but growth in a maturing category increasingly depends on volume/price trade-offs (management already flagged a 2025 mix shift toward more price pressure and gross-to-net deductions).

business.risk: Weak recent pipeline conversion / R&D execution
business.description: 2025-2026 saw multiple high-profile setbacks: tolebrutinib (BTK inhibitor for non-relapsing SPMS) received an FDA Complete Response Letter in January 2026 citing severe drug-induced liver injury (6 cases among ~2,700 patients, including one death) that the FDA said were 'among the highest in the class'; amlitelimab was discontinued in atopic dermatitis in July 2026 despite positive phase 3 data, on grounds it would not sufficiently differentiate from Dupixent/existing biologics; itepekimab (COPD, CRSwNP) and balinatunfib (IBD) programs were discontinued; riliprubart's CIDP phase 3 (MOBILIZE) was also discontinued. This is a meaningfully worse hit rate than the company's own late-2025 pipeline review implied.

FY2025 vaccines sales were roughly flat (-1.2% at CER) and 2026 guidance calls for slightly negative full-year vaccines growth (Q3-2026 guided low-to-mid-teens decline) on weaker US immunization rates and a high flu-season comparison base; Beyfortus (RSV) faces new competition from Merck's clesrovimab (Enflonsia).

financial.description: With ~51% of sales in the US, a weaker dollar is a direct earnings headwind; management's own FY2026 guidance embeds an estimated ~-1% sales and ~-2% business EPS currency drag at July 2026 average exchange rates.

Net debt rose from EUR8.8bn to EUR11.0bn over 2025 even after ~EUR10.4bn of Opella proceeds, because ~EUR12.0bn was spent on BD/M&A (Blueprint Medicines, Vigil Neuroscience, Dynavax) and ~EUR5.0bn on buybacks; Sanofi intends to retain its Aa3/AA credit ratings but has less balance-sheet slack than before the Opella sale.

regulatory.risk: US drug pricing policy (IRA, Medicare negotiation, MFN)
regulatory.description: Dupixent and other large Sanofi products are exposed to future Medicare price-negotiation rounds under the Inflation Reduction Act, and the current US administration's 'most favored nation' pricing push targets exactly the kind of premium-priced biologics that dominate Sanofi's US mix.

An April 2026 presidential proclamation set a 100% tariff on patented pharmaceutical products/APIs effective end-July 2026 for large companies without qualifying US manufacturing plans (20% for those with approved onshoring plans, rising toward 100% over four years); Sanofi is among ~13 manufacturers that have pledged large-scale US manufacturing/R&D investment to mitigate exposure, but execution and cost implications are still unfolding.

RFK Jr.-era changes to ACIP membership and the childhood immunization schedule created significant uncertainty in early 2026 (a January 2026 memorandum reduced routine childhood vaccine recommendations and stayed 2025 ACIP votes); litigation has since pushed back against some of these changes, but the episode illustrates elevated US vaccine-policy risk. Sanofi maintains Beyfortus recommendations are unaffected, but the broader erosion of public confidence in vaccination is a real headwind to industry volumes.

Depakine (sodium valproate) litigation in France remains active — 79+ families/133 individuals with civil claims as of end-2024, some cases before the French Supreme Court/Paris Court of Appeal, plus a French criminal probe into birth-defect risk disclosure; Sanofi also carries legacy Zantac/ranitidine litigation exposure in the US and other jurisdictions.

macro.risk: Rate/FX sensitivity via US dollar revenue translation
macro.description: As above; a structurally weaker dollar compounds pricing pressure.
Pharma demand is largely non-discretionary, but payer budget pressure in a slower macro environment can tighten formulary access and increase rebate demands.

execution.description: The board declined to renew CEO Paul Hudson's mandate; his last day was February 17, 2026. Belén Garijo (former Merck KGaA CEO) took over as CEO from the April 2026 AGM, with Olivier Charmeil serving as interim CEO in between. Garijo has already made an R&D leadership change (new Head of R&D, Michael Quigley, alongside Paulo Fontoura) and pushed decisive pipeline pruning (amlitelimab, itepekimab, balinatunfib) within her first 12 weeks — a new focused Executive Committee takes effect September 1, 2026. Strategy continuity, further BD/M&A discipline, and relationship management with Regeneron are all live open questions under new leadership.

Roughly EUR12bn was deployed on BD/M&A in 2025 (Blueprint Medicines, Vigil Neuroscience) plus the ~$2.2-2.5bn Dynavax deal closed February 2026; successfully integrating multiple biotech acquisitions while sustaining R&D productivity is an execution risk, especially amid leadership change.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global branded biopharma is expected to grow mid-single-digits over the next several years, with immunology/biologics and rare disease outgrowing traditional primary care and vaccines; US policy uncertainty (IRA pricing, tariffs, vaccine policy) is currently the dominant industry overhang for large-cap pharma with US exposure.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low — pharmaceutical demand is largely non-discretionary and defensive, though vaccines have meaningful seasonal/tender-driven variability and are now also exposed to policy-driven demand swings
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate — Sanofi's AA-rated balance sheet means debt service costs are manageable, but higher rates increase the discount rate applied to long-duration pipeline/NPV valuations and raise the cost of continued M&A-funded growth
key_input_costs: Biologics manufacturing capacity and raw materials (cell culture media, single-use bioreactor components)
Profit-sharing and royalty payments to partners (Regeneron for Dupixent, AstraZeneca for Beyfortus, Alnylam for Amvuttra)
US tariff exposure on imported APIs/finished products

recent_developments.event: Q2 2026 results: net sales +17.8% to EUR11.6bn, business EPS +33.3% to EUR2.09, business operating margin 28.4%; management upgraded FY2026 guidance to ~10% CER sales growth (from high-single-digit) and business EPS growth 'slightly faster than sales', and raised the 2030 Dupixent ambition to ~EUR25bn (from ~EUR22bn) and total 2030 sales ambition by ~10%.

Sanofi discontinued development of amlitelimab (anti-OX40L) in atopic dermatitis and will not pursue global regulatory submissions, despite positive long-term ESTUARY phase 3 extension data, citing insufficient differentiation from existing standard of care; company reaffirmed no change to FY2026 guidance from the decision.

Belén Garijo formally took over as CEO at the Annual General Meeting, succeeding interim CEO Olivier Charmeil; new, more focused Executive Committee effective September 1, 2026, including a new Head of R&D (Michael Quigley) working alongside Paulo Fontoura.
Sanofi's board declined to renew Paul Hudson's CEO mandate (last day Feb 17, 2026); the move was reported as the board seeking greater rigor/accountability after a run of pipeline setbacks.
Completed the acquisition of Dynavax Technologies (HEPLISAV-B adult hepatitis B vaccine plus a shingles vaccine candidate and pipeline), adding an adult-vaccines platform to the Vaccines business.

FDA issued a Complete Response Letter for tolebrutinib in non-relapsing secondary progressive MS, citing an unmitigated risk of severe drug-induced liver injury; six DILI cases (including one death) were identified among ~2,700 trial patients.

US federal vaccine-policy turmoil: a memorandum narrowed the routine childhood immunization schedule and stayed 2025 ACIP votes (thimerosal removal, COVID-19 downgrade, hepatitis B birth-dose limits); subsequent litigation pushed back on some changes. Sanofi stated Beyfortus recommendations remain unaffected but flagged a softer US vaccines demand backdrop for 2026.
Announced the ~$2.2-2.5bn acquisition of Dynavax Technologies (announced Dec-2025, closed Feb-2026).

FY2025 results: net sales EUR43,626m (+9.9% CER), business operating income EUR12,149m, free cash flow ~EUR9.9bn (18.5% of sales), net debt rose to EUR11.0bn (from EUR8.8bn) after EUR10.4bn Opella proceeds were more than offset by ~EUR12.0bn of BD/M&A and EUR5.0bn of buybacks; 31st consecutive annual dividend increase to EUR3.92/share; original 2026 guidance issued (high-single-digit CER sales growth, business EPS growing 'slightly faster than sales', EUR1bn 2026 buyback).

Completed the ~$9.5bn acquisition of Blueprint Medicines (Ayvakit/avapritinib for systemic mastocytosis) and the Vigil Neuroscience acquisition, redeploying Opella sale proceeds into Rare Disease/Immunology pipeline expansion.

items.notes: Upgraded from prior 'high single-digit percentage' guidance issued at Q4/FY2025 results (Jan-2026); a currency impact of approximately -1% on sales is anticipated at July 2026 average exchange rates.

items.target: Slightly faster than sales growth (before share buyback), i.e. low-double-digit-plus
items.notes: Prior guidance was 'low double-digit percentage' before buyback; currency impact of approximately -2% on business EPS anticipated. H1-2026 business EPS already +22.7% YoY to EUR3.97.
H1-2026 business gross margin was 79.6% at actual rates (+1.9pp reported, underlying +>1pp), driven by product mix and a Sarclisa SC provision reversal.
Full EUR1bn 2026 programme had been completed in the open market as of April 29, 2026, following EUR5bn completed in 2025.
Guided up from FY2025 effective tax rate (~19-21% range through 2025) due to pipeline changes; H1-2026 effective tax rate was 21.8%.

items.target: R&D: moderate increase (ex-discontinuation costs and potential BD/M&A); SG&A: increase to support growth/launches; G&A stable ex-exceptional items and BD/M&A
items.notes: Operating expense framework reiterated at Q2-2026; R&D H1-2026 impacted by pipeline wind-down costs (tolebrutinib, amlitelimab, itepekimab, balinatunfib) and 2025 acquisitions.
Up from prior ~EUR22bn ambition; part of a total 2030 sales ambition upgrade of ~10% at CER, roughly half currency-driven and half from underlying business performance/mix.
Risk-adjusted net sales at CER of all Pharma launches since 2019 plus limited late-stage pipeline contribution.
Down from prior ~EUR10bn ambition, reflecting the softer US vaccines demand/policy backdrop.

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Belen Garijo, in her first quarterly earnings call, emphasized 'increased focus on cost discipline,' 'sustained profitable growth with increased focus on cash generation,' and reaffirmed capital allocation priorities including the dividend and 32nd year of increases. She also signaled decisive pipeline pruning (discontinuing amlitelimab, itepekimab, balinatunfib) as part of a broader R&D transformation and 'ongoing strategic assessment of the pipeline,' alongside early discussions with Regeneron on further collaboration and stated ambitions to expand in China. CFO Francois-Xavier Roger flagged an estimated FY2026 FX impact of approximately -1% on sales and -2% on business EPS at July 2026 average exchange rates, and noted the Regeneron development balance was fully reimbursed by the end of Q2 2026, while the Amvuttra royalty from Alnylam is expected to increase ~EUR500m over 2025.

bull_case: Dupixent's 2030 ambition was just raised to ~EUR25bn and the franchise still shows >37% US growth and >1.5m patients globally with nine-plus approved indications, giving multi-year visibility even before considering lifecycle extensions (Q4W dosing, new indications)

The post-2019 launch cohort (Ayvakit, ALTUVIIIO, Sarclisa, Wayrilz, Qfitlia) is compounding at 30-60%+ growth rates and was already ~13% of Q2-2026 sales, providing a credible second growth engine as Dupixent eventually matures

Margin expansion is real and ongoing — business gross margin expanded ~3.7pp YoY in Q2-2026 and business EPS is guided to grow faster than sales, with a EUR1bn 2026 buyback and 31+ years of dividend growth returning capital alongside reinvestment

New CEO Belen Garijo (ex-Merck KGaA) has moved quickly and decisively to prune underperforming pipeline assets and refocus the Executive Committee, which could improve capital allocation discipline and R&D productivity going forward

Valuation discount versus US large-cap pharma peers (Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly, AstraZeneca) leaves room for re-rating if execution improves and Dupixent-driven upgrades continue; average analyst price targets (~EUR94-105) imply meaningful upside from the current ~EUR77 share price
bear_case: Extreme single-molecule concentration: Dupixent is ~36% of sales and the majority of growth, is profit-shared with Regeneron (capping upside), and faces direct competition from Lilly's Ebglyss and other IL-13/type-2 biologics eating into a maturing atopic dermatitis category

A genuinely poor recent R&D hit rate — tolebrutinib's FDA rejection on a serious liver-injury signal, amlitelimab's discontinuation despite positive phase 3 data, and multiple other program discontinuations (itepekimab, balinatunfib, riliprubart CIDP) — raises real questions about pipeline quality and R&D governance, which is precisely what triggered the CEO change

US policy risk is unusually high and multi-pronged simultaneously: IRA Medicare price negotiation and MFN pricing pressure, Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs (100% for firms without qualifying US manufacturing plans from July 2026), and a chaotic 2026 shift in ACIP/childhood vaccine policy that is already denting US vaccines demand and 2030 vaccines ambition (cut to ~EUR9bn from ~EUR10bn)

Leadership transition risk: a new, external CEO (first outside hire in years) is only months into the role, with a wholesale Executive Committee refresh effective September 2026 — strategy continuity, further BD/M&A discipline and the critical Regeneron relationship are all open questions

Rising net debt (EUR11.0bn, up from EUR8.8bn) after EUR12bn of 2025 BD/M&A spending, ongoing litigation overhangs (Depakine in France, legacy Zantac exposure), and persistent EUR/USD currency drag (guided -2% on FY2026 business EPS) compound the execution risk at a time the pipeline needs to deliver
